parsed.explanation: The parent regime applies directly: foreign documents are accepted, gender expression is lawful, anti-discrimination and transphobia-aggravation laws exist, and no facility or presentation ban reaches visitors. The main documented exposure is custody placement by identity-document marker, which can put trans detainees whose papers do not match in men's facilities; the 2021 watchdog opinion documents persistent, unremedied serious violations — but its evidence is mainland-based, extended to the island only by law, and no island-specific detention or violence data exists. Most other material (LGR procedure, labour code, healthcare access, youth-care debate) is resident-facing climate, not traveller exposure. Local recourse is thin (no referenced LGBT-friendly lawyer) and the predominantly Muslim island context suggests social friction beyond written law, though documented only via one marriage case. Extrapolating thin data from the structural signals: functioning national legal framework, no trans-specific criminalisation, documented custody-violation pattern without shown remedy. This sits between the reduced-risk tier (working protections, acceptance) and elevated risk (an unremedied universal custody exposure): mid-0.60s territory, slightly discounted for local recourse gaps — 0.60.
